prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No fleet of turbines has AI blade control that adapts in real time to every gust, and the Main KPI of 1,000,000 turbines upgraded is not met (it exceeds today's global turbine count, so it implies new and retrofitted turbines). Active trailing-edge flaps and morphing blades remain field and rig tests (DTU INDUFLAP on a 100 kW turbine, Sandia SMART rotor, https://www.windpower-international.com/analysis/more-than-a-flap-in-the-wind-smart-blade-control-and-flap-systems-4623534/; Limerick outdoor rig, https://pure.ul.ie/en/publications/field-testing-of-morphing-flaps-on-a-wind-turbine-blade-using-an-/). AI pitch-control retrofits are patents and single-turbine studies without a fleet count (https://www.windsystemsmag.com/the-application-of-ai-across-wind-energy/). Honest limit: individual pitch control is already in many commercial turbines, and open controllers implement IPC and lidar feedforward (NREL ROSCO, https://rosco.readthedocs.io/; Russell et al. 2024, up to 12% load gain in simulation, https://strathprints.strath.ac.uk/88862). Tasks that re-implement IPC or lidar feedforward are not new; work must target unsolved gust-resolved blade actuation, its reliability, or field-validated learned control with its own prior-art basis.
